Based on the provided bug report, the issue is related to the `ratio` parameter in the `ImageArcGISRest` source of OpenLayers 7.4. The default value of this parameter is set to 1.5, which can lead to layer-map mismatches when the zoom or scaling ratio is not 100%. The report suggests that the workaround is to set the ratio to 1 to avoid these issues.

### Bug Analysis
The root cause of the bug is the default value of the `ratio_` property in the `ImageArcGISRest` class. When the ratio is set to values other than 1, it can cause misalignment of the layers with the map, especially when the map is rotated or when the zoom level is not at 100%. 

### Bug Code Snippets Analysis
The relevant code snippets are located in the `src/ol/source/ImageArcGISRest.js` file, where the `ratio_` is initialized in the constructor. The code snippet that needs to be modified is:

```javascript
this.ratio_ = options.ratio !== undefined ? options.ratio : 1.5;
```

This line should be changed to set the default ratio to 1 instead of 1.5.

### Patches
Here are the patches to fix the bug:

```javascript
### src/ol/source/ImageArcGISRest.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
    this.ratio_ = options.ratio !== undefined ? options.ratio : 1.5;
=======
    this.ratio_ = options.ratio !== undefined ? options.ratio : 1;
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

This change will ensure that the default ratio is set to 1, which should resolve the layer-map mismatch issues described in the bug report.
